title: Kenyan Coconut Bhajia
community: Swahili — a coastal variation of the classic bhajia
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Coastal Coconut Bhajia — the Swahili coast's own version of bhajia, where coconut milk replaces water in the gram flour batter, adding a subtle sweetness and rich coconut fragrance to the crispy fried potato slices. A coastal elevation of the classic street snack.
longDesc: Bajias za Nazi takes the beloved bhajia and gives it a distinctly coastal character — replacing the water in the batter with coconut milk, adding cardamom, and finishing with a tamarind coconut chutney. The result is a bhajia with a subtle sweetness and coconut aroma that perfectly complements the crispy potato and the tangy chutney.
steps: Slice potatoes 2—3mm thin. Pat completely dry.
Combine gram flour, rice flour, spices, cardamom, salt, and baking powder.
Whisk in coconut milk gradually. Add water if needed to reach a medium-thick batter.
Dip potato slices in coconut batter. Fry in batches for 3—4 minutes until golden.
Drain on a rack. Serve with tamarind coconut chutney.
chefTips: Coconut milk makes the batter slightly thicker — adjust water accordingly.
The cardamom is the coastal signature — do not skip it.
Serve with the tamarind coconut chutney from KEN017.
commonMistakes: Wet potato slices — batter does not adhere.
cookingScience: Replacing water with coconut milk adds fat to the batter, which produces a slightly more tender, less brittle crust than the classic water-based version — a pleasant coastal variation.
sustainabilityTips: Coconut milk from locally grown coastal coconuts is the most sustainable choice.
healthBenefits: Gram flour provides plant protein and fibre.
culturalNote: Bajias za Nazi represent the Swahili coast's instinct to add coconut to everything — transforming the already-beloved bhajia into something distinctly, fragrantly coastal.
